claims.statement: For the complexification of the real 16-dimensional Spin(9) spinor, the four nontrivial Clifford-grade squared moments of a pure state are (s1,s2,s3,s4)=(p+(1-p)t,(1-p)(1+3t),(1-p)(7-3t),7(1+p)-(1-p)t), with p,t in [0,1]. The exact moment image is the triangle with vertices vH=(0,1,7,7), vV=(1,4,4,6), and vR=(1,0,0,14).
assumptions: Real symmetric Spin(9) Clifford generators with the stated grade normalization.
Standard transitive Spin(9) spinor-sphere action, Spin(7) stabilizer, and octonionic Hopf geometry.
The Spin(6) stabilizer action on the remaining real 8-dimensional spinor summand is the real form of the defining SU(4) action.
claims.support_statement: Every point of the triangle is attained by the explicit seed family in pure_orbits.md; the grade-two and grade-three coefficients are derived from exact Clifford/Casimir and octonionic-model calculations.
claims.novelty_boundary: The orbit geometry and Hopf fibration are standard. The search was bounded and makes no novelty or priority claim for the moment calculation.
claims.costs: Closed finite-dimensional algebra; no data acquisition or approximate numerical optimization.
claims.falsifier: An incorrect orbit classification, Clifford normalization, grade-three coefficient, or explicit seed attaining a moment outside the stated triangle falsifies the claim.
claims.next_gate: Independent mathematical review of the orbit/Casimir derivation; extension to other spinor dimensions is not established.

claims.statement: For every invariant dual Q=sum(alpha_k Pi_k) with alpha_k>=0, the support over full-domain canonical EB channels is S_can(Q)=max{alpha1+14 alpha4, alpha2+7 alpha3+7 alpha4, alpha1+4 alpha2+4 alpha3+6 alpha4}.
assumptions: Canonical measure-and-prepare means each POVM effect is prepared in its normalized state.
Spin(9)-orbit POVMs are normalized with effects 16 P_g dg and preparations P_g.
Higher-rank canonical effects are bounded for this positive score by convex refinement of squared expectations.
claims.support_statement: Each support vertex is attained by a full-domain orbit POVM. This is a positive-dual support identity, not a claim that every canonical EB transfer vector belongs to the pure-seed triangle or a bound on unrestricted noncanonical EB channels.
claims.novelty_boundary: Group twirling and measure-and-prepare channels are standard; no priority claim is made.
claims.costs: Haar-orbit existence proof; no finite-outcome implementation cost is asserted.
claims.falsifier: A canonical EB POVM with positive invariant score greater than the displayed maximum, or a failure of the claimed orbit POVM normalization, falsifies the support identity.
claims.next_gate: A finite-outcome exact implementation of the Spin(9) orbit comparators is not supplied here.

claims.statement: For every alpha in R_+^4, the full ordinary-tensor Spin(9) star satisfies lambda_max(H(alpha)) <= 9 alpha1+36 alpha2+84 alpha3+126 alpha4+S_can(Q), including both output-swap signs.
assumptions: The stated Spin(9) triple-product decomposition with multiplicities 5,4,3,2,1 is complete.
The Clifford-word star matrices and exact highest-weight restriction code match the declared Choi/star convention.
The canonical-EB support identity above is used as the support function on each cone.
claims.support_statement: Exact cone rays are checked in all nine isotypic/swap blocks by all principal minors. The total dimension 4096 and swap dimensions 2176/1920 are retained. The isotropic top eigenvalue is 270.
claims.novelty_boundary: Universal cloning and representation reduction are standard controls. A bounded search found no directly matching result but yields no novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: Exact SymPy arithmetic; nine multiplicity blocks; ten exact support-cone rays; no floating-point SDP grid. This is not formal proof-assistant verification.
claims.falsifier: A missing representation block, omitted swap sign, negative exact principal minor, or incorrect cone ray falsifies the certificate.
claims.next_gate: Independent reproduction from a separately derived Spin(9) decomposition or a formalized proof remains desirable.

claims.statement: Every Spin(9)-covariant unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint channel on the complexified 16-dimensional spinor with a two-output CPTP extension having both marginals equal to the channel admits one full-domain canonical EB channel Psi with Psi >= 2 Phi - id on the Hermitian operator space.
assumptions: The input/output representation is the complexified real 16-dimensional irreducible Spin(9) spinor.
Phi is CPTP, unital, trace preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint, and Spin(9)-covariant.
A CPTP two-output extension exists with both one-site marginals equal to Phi.
The order is positive-semidefinite order on the real Hilbert space of Hermitian matrices.
claims.support_statement: The positive-dual inequalities and convex separation yield one comparator on the full matrix domain. The construction is not a collection of statewise witnesses or sectorwise comparators.
claims.novelty_boundary: No external novelty review was performed. The bounded source search is not priority evidence. The result is restricted to this covariant Spin(9) class.
claims.costs: Proof-level existence result. No efficient finite-outcome compiler or experimental implementation is provided.
claims.falsifier: A legal channel satisfying the assumptions for which every full-domain canonical EB Psi violates Psi >= 2 Phi - id is a direct counterexample.
claims.next_gate: Arbitrary noncovariant channels, other irreducible representations, and the bounded-Holevo/vanishing-broadcast-error implication remain UNKNOWN.

checks: Exact rational/nullspace enumeration gives six rays for each of the three support cones.
The union contains ten distinct rays.
All 4096 dimensions are covered by the isotypic decomposition.
Both output-swap signs are retained: dimensions 2176 and 1920.
All exact principal minors are nonnegative at all ten rays in all nine blocks.
The full isotropic star top eigenvalue is 270.
All 45 independent real Clifford relations (nine squares and 36 cross-anticommutators) hold exactly in the integer matrix model.
The grade-three nonzero coefficient sets match the four vertical and seven horizontal Fano triples in pure_orbits.md.
The resulting coefficients are B3(vertical)=4 and B3(horizontal)=7.
